sections.h2: Selling a Del Rio house without a long wait
sections.html:
A broker's listing, a sale you manage yourself and a quick deal with a cash purchaser are the three choices. Listings take longer to turn up a buyer, whereas cash gives you the say over when you close.

Before you talk price, round up the deed, a payoff letter from your lender, your newest tax bill and whatever permit records you have. Every written offer needs to name the price and closing date, say who covers title and recording costs, and describe the condition the buyer wants at handover.

  • Check if the buyer plans an inspection before the offer becomes firm.
  • Decide whether furniture and appliances stay or go.
  • Have the closing date written down.

sections.h2: What buyers see in Del Rio housing
sections.html: Del Rio lies on U.S. Highway 90 at the spot where the Rio Grande and San Felipe Creek meet, 154 miles west of San Antonio. It incorporated on November 15, 1911, and counted 33,867 people in 2000. The oldest homes sit near the creek. Housing later shifted north of the rail line, and the retail strip along Highway 90 and the reservoir built in the 1960s tugged growth north once more. Describe your block with that pattern in mind, and refer school zoning questions to the school district.

sections.h2: Permit steps for a home project
sections.html:
The Development Services Department reviews plans and issues building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, sign and garage sale permits. Its inspectors also look at substandard buildings, and it grants certificates of occupancy.

Del Rio enforces the 2024 editions of the International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Plumbing, Fire, Energy Conservation and Fuel and Gas codes, together with the 2024 Property Maintenance Code and the 2020 National Electrical Code. A garage conversion or addition built with no permit should be disclosed to the buyer, and the city can explain how to close that file.

sections.h2: Val Verde County tax bills at closing
sections.html:
Values are set as of January 1, and the lien for the year attaches the same day. Bills go in the mail around October 1. Owners may split payment, with half due by November 30 and half by June 30, although most bills must be paid by January 31.

Property records sit with the Val Verde County appraisal district and tax office, and the city home page links to its tax department. A seller who never claimed a homestead exemption leaves that option open to a buyer closing later in the year. Your closing statement should show the year's bill divided between you and the buyer, so check that line.

sections.h2: Selling a rental that has a tenant
sections.html:
If a tenant refuses to go, Texas expects the landlord to follow a fixed order. First comes a written demand to vacate. Three days is the default unless the lease names a different period. Next the landlord files in justice court, the tenant is served at least four days before trial, and the hearing is set somewhere between 10 and 21 days after the filing date.

The losing side has five days from judgment to appeal to county court. When no appeal stops it, a writ of possession becomes available six days after the final judgment. An officer then has five days to serve it, and the tenant receives 24 hours of warning before being removed. People who buy occupied houses will want the lease, deposit records and rent history. Some owners sell with the lease still running, and a landlord going that way should talk with the tenant early about showings.

A will can be probated by heirs up to four years after the owner dies. Where no administration is needed, a muniment of title may be enough. With no will, a small estate affidavit works only if the assets come to $75,000 or less and every heir agrees. An owner who signed and filed a transfer on death deed during life leaves a house that skips probate.

Lenders on a defaulted loan usually wait out the first 120 days of missed payments. After that you get 20 days to catch up, and the lender has to post notice of the auction at least three weeks ahead of the first Tuesday on which it sells. Money left over after the lender is paid goes to junior liens and then to you. Begin by asking the servicer for an exact payoff.

sections.h2: City permits and licenses that can touch a sale
sections.html:
Development Services also hands out garage sale and sign permits, so an estate sale or moving sale may require one. The city has a business license service as well, and its business pages carry a hotel occupancy tax application for lodging operators. If guests ever stayed in the house by the night, ask whether those pages apply to you before closing.

Utilities run through the city, which handles billing and residential waste collection. Get a final bill and a stop-service date so the buyer begins with a clean account.

Cleaning out the house before closing is also on you. If a sale leaves furniture, a vehicle or yard debris behind, the buyer may hold back money or refuse to close. Decide early what stays, and take photos of the empty rooms once the work is finished.

sections.h2: Filing the deed and closing day
sections.html: The Val Verde County Clerk records the deed after a notary has acknowledged it. Most title companies file it for you and pay the recording charge from the settlement funds. Closing day means signing the deed and a settlement statement, turning over keys and openers, and collecting what is left after the loan payoff and the tax share.

sections.h2: Questions to put to each buyer
sections.html:
Judge bids on more than price. Ask how each buyer is paying, how soon they can close and whether they expect repairs. Proof of funds and a written date are worth more than a bigger number resting on a loan nobody has checked.

Ask, too, who picks the title company and who pays for the owner's title policy, since those two answers change what you take home. If the house is rented, say so to every bidder at the start and hand over the lease in your first conversation, not after a contract exists.

faqs.q: Does Del Rio require a permit for home repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, when the work falls under the adopted codes: building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and sign work. Development Services reviews plans, issues permits, inspects and signs off with a certificate of occupancy.

faqs.q: Who buys houses in Del Rio?
faqs.a: Local families, military households, landlords and cash purchasers all shop here. Offers from a financed buyer, an agent's advice and a cash quote will show you who is active at your price.

faqs.q: Which office files a Del Rio deed?
faqs.a: The Val Verde County Clerk, once the signature has been properly acknowledged. Your title company typically files it and pays the fee from closing funds.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Del Rio eviction finish?
faqs.a: Figure on several weeks. The hearing is set 10 to 21 days after filing, removal by an officer waits until at least six days after judgment, and notice, service and any appeal all take time.

faqs.q: Can Del Rio heirs sell without full probate?
faqs.a: In some cases. Heirs may be able to use a small estate affidavit, a muniment of title, or a transfer on death deed the owner filed in life. A title company can tell you which of these a buyer will accept.
